goal_frame: Monitor ONE concrete goal - protect value and margin while growing sales - and the rules and emergent culture around discounting. Not comprehensive monitoring of the organization.

rule_status_key.proposed_unapproved: mandate-v2-draft / codex-v2: every discount receives an explicit customer commitment in return (preview only)
rule_status_key.training_norms: unapproved SOP/training norms, not binding rules

stage_key: request (customer asks) / offer (seller states terms) / grant (seller agrees in-episode) / refusal / accepted_deal / payment. Grant in a chat is NOT an accepted deal and NOT a payment; CRM linkage for these episodes is unestablished.

rules_reviewed.statement: Founder principle: business prefers gifts; discounts suit the economy segment.
Partner 30% applies only to self-launched solutions, not the club tariff; broad wording prohibited.
SOP: the manager never bargains directly; escalates and returns with a gift instead of a discount.
SOP: never name the price in the first message.
Unified price intended; deviations only via sales head (same note records live price scatter).

observed_examples_reviewed.statement: Partner requests a discount when launching two companies (2024-04-24).
Seller agrees immediately at 10k in the same conversation; per-branch basis not explicit.
Seller grants an extra 30% off platform price (2026-08-13); payment route asked next.
Seller mentions partner 30% without stating its scope (2026-09-22).
Announced loyalty discount not applied; client paid full price, fix promised (2026-06-19, archive-summary based).

counterexamples_reviewed.statement: Bulk-review discount request refused: minimum price (2025-05-27).
Scope correction exists and is communicated to partners.
Price-ladder template sits in the same SOP source that forbids price-first messages.

narration_safe_lines: We watch one goal: protect value and margin while growing sales.
The proposed rule - every discount earns a customer commitment in return - is still unapproved; today flexible seller discounts are the active baseline.
In the reviewed episodes, discounts are granted case by case, sometimes immediately, and the commitment in return is not recorded; firm refusals at minimum price also occur.
External review found no proven contradiction - it found a monitoring gap: discount outcomes and reasons are not captured, so compliance can be neither proven nor disproven at scale.
